FIFTY-NINTH ANNUAL REPORT 
OF THE BOARD OF 
DIRECTORS 


a most eventful one in the history of the Association. 
The enlargement of the Central Building has been an 
issue with the Board of Directors for the past five years, but no 
satisfactory solution seemed possible until April of last year, 
when a Building Campaign was carefully planned, on the lines 
suggested by Mr. C. 8S. Ward, Secretary of the International 
Committee. 

An Executive Committee was formed, under the Chair- 
manship of our President, Mr. John W. Ross, ably assisted by 
Messrs. R. C. Holden, W. M. Birks, F. Howard Wilson, C. C. 
Holland, Gerald W. Birks, L. H. Packard, R. L. Charlton, and 
J. W. McConnell. 

This Committee held at least two meetings each week for 
two months, prior to June 9th, the date of the opening of the 
campaign. A Citizens’ Committee was formed, with Mr. W. 
M. Birks as Chairman; also a Young Business Men’s Commit- 
tee of ten teams, with Mr. J. W. McConnell as Chairman, and 
a Young Men’s Committee, consisting of ten teams. 

An initial subscription of $25,000 was generously made by 
Messrs. Henry Birks & Sons. The Campaign lasted thirteen 
days, and with the hearty co-operation of the two hundred 
volunteer workers, the citizens, and the press, the Building 
Fund closed with 3,419 subscribers and a grand total of 
$321,749.39, made up as follows: 


iG Bie YEAR which closed on April 30th, 1910, has been

$321,749 39 


Of this amount $150,693.58 has been received in cash, up 
to May 16th. Two further payments become due in Septem- 
ber, 1910, and in March, 1911. 

In connection with the Building Campaign we have to 
report a subscription made by one of our Directors, the late 
Mr. David Yuile, on the eve of his leaving for the Johns 
Hopkins Hospital, in Baltimore. He telephoned a subserip- 
tion of $5,000.00, to be devoted to the Foreign Work Fund of 
the Young Men’s Christian Association. This amount has 
been invested in the Foreign Work Fund, through the advice 
of Mr. John R. Mott, of New York. 

Immediately at the close of the campaign a Building 
Committee was appointed, composed of Mr. Rufus C. Holden, 
Chairman, Messrs. John W. Ross, C. C. Holland, Gerald W. 
Birks, L. H. Packard, John Kennedy, H. R. MacGregor, 
Lemuel Cushing, and R. B. Ross, Jr. 

This Commitee has held two regular meetings each week, 
since last June, and carefully formulated plans. 


Central Building—So many and so serious difficulties 
arose in regard to the remodelling and enlargement of the 
Central Building, Dominion Square, that the Committee 
finally decided that.the future interests of the Association 
would be served to the best advantage by going forward with 
a new building, and with the consent of the Board of Directors 
the property was advertised for sale. 


4 


Finally an offer of $250,000, from the Sun Life Assurance 
Company, for the Central Building, was accepted by the 
Board of Directors, and a new site purchased on Drummond 
Street, just above St. Catherine, at a cost of $70,000. This 
site contains ample room for the proposed Central Building, 
and for future extension. 

After securing the property on Drummond Street our 
solicitors advised that, in order to insure an absolutely clear 
title, it would be necessary to seeure an Act of Parliament, 
through the Quebec Legislature. This was immediately 
undertaken by our Directors, and we are now awaiting the 
final passing of this Act. 

Work has begun in the excavation and foundation on the 
Drummond Street Building. 

The thanks of this Association are due to the Executive 
Committee, who carried the Building Campaign to such a 
splendid success, and to the present Building Committee, 
under the chairmanship of Mr. R. C. Holden, who have given 
so much time and thought to the preparation of plans, and 
other important matters concerning the erection of the three 
new buildings. 

Westmount.—A site on the corner of Arlington Avenue 
and Sherbrooke Street, was secured at a cost of $9,456.00, and 
the plans for a Branch Building on this lot are now in pro- 
cess of completion. 

Fairmount.—A site on the corner of Park Avenue and St. 
Viateur Street, was purchased at a cost of $7,182.50. Plans 
for a Branch Building on this site have passed the Committee, 
and are now in the architect’s hands for completion. 

The Building Committee hope to be able to have the West- 
mount and Fairmount Branch Buildings ready to open in the 
fall of 1911. 

This will give the Association a new Central Building and 
three Branch Buildings well situated, so as to meet the rapid 
growth of the city, and the Board of Directors realize the 
great responsibility which is involved in carrying forward 
three new building projects at the same time. 

Your Directors expect to place a Secretary in the East End 
section of the city this fall. In this way they hope to dis- 
cover how the Association can best serve the young men in 
that section of the city. 

They desire here to record their gratitude to God for His 
blessing, and for the success of the Campaign, making possible 
this advance movement for our city, and we also wish to 
thank the citizens, and the press, for their most generous 
*to-operation. 


Reports will be presented to-night by the Central, Railroad, 
and Fairmount Branches, and MeGill College Association. 
The Board of Directors wish to thank the Committee of Man- 
agement of these Branches for the helpful service they have 
rendered during the year. 

Notwithstanding the added financial strain, caused by the 
two payments called for by the Building Fund, the Finance 
Committee is able to report all bills paid on current expense 
accounts at each of the Branches and a small balance carried 
forward. 


Vacation Camps—A new site has been secured for the 
Boys’ Camp on Lake Kanawana, near Shawbridge, in the 
Laurentian Mountains. A complete camping equipment is 
now being purchased, and a Committee representing the three 
Branches is completing the plans for a summer vacation 
camp for boys, from July 1st to August 15th. They will have 
accommodation for 70 boys. This camp will be under the 
charge of Mr. W. J. Holliday, of the Central Branch. 

The Summer Camp at Lac St. Joseph will have renewed 
equipment, and will be given over entirely to the senior mem- 
bers. A Committee representing all the Branches will pro- 
mote this camp, with J. E. Merritt officer in charge. 

This ideal vacation camp opportunity now made possible 
for both senior and junior members, in all the city Branches, 
should greatly strengthen the summer programme of the 
Association. 


The Orkney Estate Bequest—As one of the three 
residuary legatees of the estate of the late Miss Elizabeth 
Orkney, the Association has received the following shares of 
stock and cash: 27 shares Bank of Montreal, 68 shares Molsons 
Bank, 53 shares Bank of Toronto, 200 shares Montreal Tele- 
graph Company, 147 shares Bell Telephone Company, 45 
shares Montreal Street Railway Company, also in cash 
$4,295.10. 

The Directors have decided to hand this fund to the Build- 
ing Committee in order to make possible the larger plans for 
the Central Building. This fund to be treated as an endow- 
ment on behalf of the Board. 


Immigration.—Situated at the port of entry to the Do- 
minion, this Association makes an important contribution to 
the national life of the country. The Associations throughout 
Great Britain are sending hundreds of young men to Canada. 
At Liverpool a special secretary is employed to visit all ships 
before they sail, and place in the hands of young men cards 
of introduction to the Associations in the cities where they 


6 


plan to settle. The Montreal Association becomes the clearing 
house, and hundreds of these young men receive their first 
welcome to Canada in this building, and through the Asso- 
ciation officers. In this way we render a most important 
service in the development of our national life. 

The Board of Directors desire to recognize the hearty 
co-operation of the employed officers in all the Branches, 
which makes possible such a splendid report as will be pre- 
sented to-night. With such a force of men rendermg un- 
selfish service, they are most hopeful and confident for the 
results during the coming year. 

During the past two years we greatly regret the loss by 
death of the subscribers and members as shown on the follow- 
ing page. 


JOHN W. ROSS, 
President. 
D. A. BUDGE, 
General Secretary.

13 


Annual Report of the Committee 
of Management 


In the short time allotted to me it is not possible to describe in 
detail the work which has been so successfully carried on in every 
department, during the year just closed. All we can hope to do is 
to show up in bas-relief those things which stand out as accom- 
plishments during the year, 


Membership 


J. K. McNutt, Chairman. 
W. J. Houuipay, Secretary. 


The record made this year in this Department is one we all may 
well be proud of—the most successful winter in the history of the 
Montreal Association. 

There are three features in the report of the Membership Com- 
mittee that stand out as high-water marks: 


(1) One hundred and sixty-five more new members are re- 
ported to have joined during 1909-10 than in the previous year. In 
1909 the Committee reported a 


Total membership of.. .. .......... 1,750 
In 1910 membership of..°.. .. ...... 1,875 


(2) The percentage of expirations having renewed is 65 per cent., 
as compared with 42 per cent. last year. We believe this estab- 
lishes a record on this continent for renewals. Enquiries made 
among several Associations brought out the fact that 30 per cent. 
to 35 per cent. is the average percentage in American Associations. 

(8) The receipts for the year from this Department have ex- 
ceeded the amount asked for by the Committee of Management, by 
$170.00, as the following figures will show: 

Estimated for year. 1910. 1909. 
$8,500.00 $8,670.00 $8,071.00 

Nearly every nationality and every erced has been represented 
within the membership during the year, 


Religious 


W. H. Goopwin, Chairman. 
C. Gorpon Armowr, Secretary. 


The Young Men’s Christian Association stands squarely for the 
religious development of its membership—to have every man coming 
under its influence to intelligently recognize the claims of Christ, 
and accept Him as Lord and Saviour. With this end in view the 
following activities have been conducted: 


14 


I. SUNDAY AFTERNOON MEN’S MEETINGS 


These meetings have been held each Sunday afternoon through- 
out the year, in the Association Building. Forty-five meetings have 
been held, with a total attendance of 5,240—this making an average 
attendance per Sunday of 117 men. Besides the pastors of local 
churches, the following out-of-town speakers were secured: 

Prof. Theodore Soares, Ph.D., Chicago University. 

Rev. Balcom Shaw, of Chicago. 

Rev. Dr. Erdman, of Princeton. 

Rey. Dr. Kent, of New York. 

Dr. A. EB. Keigwin, of New York, 

Dr. Wilbur Crafts, of New York. 

Dr. Perey Leslie, of China. 

Dr. J. A. McDonald, of Toronto Globe. 

Parole Commissioner Archibald, of Ottawa. 

Principal O’Meara, of Toronto. 


II. SATURDAY NIGHT MEETING 


This meeting has been held regularly at 8 p.m. every week, with 
an average attendance of forty men. Its aim is devotional and 
evangelistic in character. A number of men have decided to lead 
the Christian life, and many have been helped and strengthened 
as a result of these meetings. 

Special thanks is due to Mr. P. A. Doig, Mr. J. S. Gibb, and the 
committee of workers for their faithful work in this Department 
during the past year. 


II. BIBLE STUDY 


The following classes have been held during the past year: 


(1) The Brotherhood Class, D. A. Budge, Leader. 

Organized October 17th, and has met every Sunday afternoon at 
three o’clock since. This class has been taking up “Great Events in 
the Life of Christ.” Twenty-seven sessions have been held, with an 
average attendance of 27. 


(2) The Gymnasium Men's Bible Study Club—Has met Sundays 
at 5.15, under’ the leadership of Mr. J. B. Merritt, taking up a 
course on “Decisions.” 


(3) Educational Students’ Bible Class has met on Sunday morn- 
ing at 9.45, under the leadership of the Educational ‘Director, Mr. 
F. G, White. 


(4) Business Men’s Bible Class,—Under leadership of Prof. C. 
E. Bland, took up course of Bosworth’s “Teachings of Jesus and His 
Apostles.” About fifteen business men met every Tuesday evening 
at 7.00 o’clock. 


(5) Personal Workers’ Class.—Under leadership of Mr. J. BE. 
Millen, which studies Howard A. Johnston’s “Training of Christian 
Workers,” and was attended by ten men. 


(6) Teachers’ Training Class.—This class, under leadership of 
Mr. Budge, and attended by eighteen men, studied See’s “Teaching of 
Bible Classes.” 


(7) “New Studies in Acts.”—Taught to a group of young men by 
W. J. Holliday. 
To sum up, seven classes were conducted, with a total average 
weekly attendance of one hundred and forty. 
15 


IV. SUMMER SONG SERVICE 


Every Sunday evening some fifty to sixty of our members 
gathered after church on the steps of the Association Building, and 
entered into a service of song, which was heard by thousands of 
men and women who thronged Dominion Square on those evenings. 
Too much praise cannot be given to Mr. Harold Smeal for his part 
in this work. 


Vv. “THE HOME HOUR” 


This was introduced into the Association by Mr. C. Gordon 
Armour as a new departure, after discontinuing the Summer Song 
Service. Every Sunday night throughout the winter months, at the 
close of the church services, from forty to sixty young men gathered 
about the fireside on the reception floor of the building, and for an 
hour all joined in the singing of their favorite hymns. Light 
refreshments were served afterwards. “The Home Hour” was 
especially arranged for “the man away from home,” and many of 
these men have said as they have gone away from the warm fireside, 
it was the most “homelike hour of the week.” 

The report of the Religious Work does not include the scores 
and scores of men who have been personally interviewed as to the 
Christian life—nor as to the many interviews and visits paid to the 
hospitals by the Committee during the year. It merely shows us the 
tremendous possibilities of this work among the young men of 
Montreal. 


Foreign Work Department 


Mr. Charles §. Paterson, a former member of our Association, 
is our representative in India, and is in charge of the Boys’ Work 
of the Calcutta Young Men’s Christian Association. Reports, which 
come to us from time to time, of Mr. Paterson’s work in India, are 
in every way encouraging, and we have great reason to believe 
that a very real service is being rendered by Mr. Paterson to the 
boys of Calcutta. 

The financial year of the International Committee is from 
January to January. For the year ending January, 1910, our 
Association remitted to the International Committee the sum of 
$1,200, this being the amount required for the support of Mr. 
Paterson. This amount was composed of voluntary donations on 
behalf of the members of our Association. For the present year, 
1910, our financial position is as follows: 


14 monthly subscriptions of from 25 cents to $2.00. .$ 93 00 
30 yearly subscriptions of from $1.00 to $100.00.. 544 00

One meeting has been held by the Foreign Work Department this 
year. This was held,during the month of April, and was attended 
by 100 business men. The meeting was addressed by Rev. Mr. 
Goforth, who gave an inspiring message to those present. Splendid 
service has been rendered in this Department by Mr. W. Y. King. 


16 


Educational Department 


W. E. CusHINnG, Chairman. 
F. G. Wuite, Secretary. 


During the year 470 different students were enrolled in the 
classes—of these 362 were in the Senior Department, and 108 in the 
Junior Department. Classes were conducted in Arithmetic, Pen- 
manship, Accountancy, Bookkeeping, Matriculation, Building Con- 
struction, Plan Reading, Steam Engineering, French, English, Com- 
mercial Law, First Aid, Shorthand, Typewriting, and Singing. 

The total registration was 537, and the total attendance 11,551. 


Examinations.—135 students wrote on the International Examin- 
ations, held April 4—9. Of these 78 were successful. 17 students 
were awarded the St. John’s Ambulance Society First Aid Certificate. 
About ten men will sit for the McGill University examinations this 
fall. 


Finances.—The amount received in class fees was $2,864.65, 
with a total expenditure of $2,463.84. This is an increase in fees 
of $500.00 over last year’s record. 


Social—Several socials were held during tne year—the Annual 
Banquet on March 31st being addressed by Professor Dale, of 
McGill, and Mr. J. Pullen, of the Grand Trunk Railway System, and 
was very successful. Another event of interest was the “May 
morning Breakfast,” under the direction of the Educational Students’ 
Bible Class, on May ist, being attended by one hundred men. 


The Literary and Debating Club—Season 1909-10.—All meetings 
were well attended, the discussions and debates, addresses, and 
impromptu speaking being’ of a character worthy of commendation. 

The Annual Inter-Club Debate with McGill University, and the 
Debate with members of the Social Committee of the Association, are 
worthy of mention. 

The Annual Dinner of the Club was held in January, and the 
season closed with an “Oratorical Contest’ for the prize kindly 
donated by the retiring President, Mr. G. L. McCrae, which, after a 
spirited display of talent by the participants, was awarded by the 
judges to Mr. E. W. Griffith. 


Library.—The Library continues to be well used, and growing 
in popularity, and the Educational Department Committee suggests 
that during the coming season the Library should be thoroughly 
overhauled, old books replaced, and a good supply of new books 
purchased. 


Physical Department 


E. C. Buper, Chairman. 
J. E. Merritt, Physical Director. 


Gymnasium Classes, as outlined in the Prospectus, have been 
held during the past year, with a total of twenty-eight weekly 
classes, and a total registration of 608. The total attendance at all 
Classes for the year is 14,698. 802 Class sessions were conducted 
with a weekly average of 501. 


17 


Besides these Classes a great many other attractions have been 
continued during the year. 

Two hundred and two boys, between the ages of 12 and 17, 
were taught to swim the length of the plunge, and a large number 
of other boys increased in their efficiency. 


The Leaders’ Corps met for special training and work every 
Saturday evening, under the direction of the Physical Director. 


The Tennis Club had a very successful season last summer, 
with a total membership of 58. The fee was increased from two 
dollars to three, to meet the expense of installing a shower bath at 
the courts. 


The Baseball Club won the championship of the Y. M. CG. A. 
League. Several out-of-town games were played. The Club had a 
total membership of 27. 


The Harrier Club continued during the year, having the use 
of the McGill tracks. A series of summer handicaps were conducted 
in July and August. The 13th Annual Field Day was also held at 
McGill grounds, and attracted considerable interest. The Club’s 
membership totals 62. 


The Basketball season was a very successful one. Eleven 
teams were entered in the Association League—six senior teams 
and five intermediate teams, the “Harriers” winning the beautiful 
trophy presented by Messrs. A. G. Spalding & Bros. . 

Three teams were entered in the City and District Basketball 
League, finishing second in the senior, and winning the champion- 
ship in the intermediate series. Several out-of-town games were 
played, Ottawa, Sherbrooke, and Quebec being visited. 


The Polo Club was organized for the first time, and entered two 
teams in the Polo Club of the city. 


The Snowshoe Club tramped regularly on Friday evenings, and 
Saturday afternoons, throughout the season. The annual “At Home” 
was well attended and enjoyed. This year the Club closed with a 
banquet, attended by forty enthusiasts. The membership reached 
a total of 83. 


A Hockey Club of 22 members was organized, which made a 
splendid start. More will be heard from this Club during the 
coming year. 


Senior Camp.—Camp opened July 17th, and closed August 30th. 

Mr. Harold Beall, a former member of the staff, was in charge 
for the whole season. 

The attendance was 75, over 40% of this number being men out 
for the first time. 

The usual camp sports and socials were held, and much enjoyed. 
Sunday services were held regularly, and were well attended, the 
collections at the services amounting to $23.41, and were donated 
to the Old Brewery Mission Summer Camp.

Employment Department 
C. Gorpon Armoor, Secretary. 


The present Secretary took charge of this work the ist of July, 
of last year. Its scope is city-wide, and its success is vividly 
shown by the report just issued, a grand total of 253 permanent 
positions being filled during the past ten months, which represented 
a monthly pay-roll of eight thousand eight hundred and seventy- 
nine dollars. The number of positions filled by this department has 
been steadily increasing, until, during the month of April, over 
sixty men were placed in permanent positions. 


Boys’ Department 


Mr. Lemuet Cusuine, Chairman. 
Mr. Murray G. Brooks, Secretary. 


The year closed, April 30th, with a total membership of 379, 
divided as follows: 


Junior School Boys.. .. .. .. .. 100 
Senior School Boys ............ 35 
Junior Business Boys .. .. .. .... 115 
Intermediate Business Boys... .... 129 

379 


The one feature standing out this year has been the formation 
of numerous Clubs within the membership, and the strong tendency 
among the boys to adopt the club system. The following were 
continued, or organized: H. A. B. Club, Busy Boys’ Club, the 
“Mooses,” “Buffaloes,” “Coyotes,” the Vics. Athletic Club, and the 
“Arrow.” 

These different Clubs were all properly organized, meeting for 
supper, Bible study, and business.” 


The Religious Work of the Department has been conducted 
largely through these Clubs. In November, a visit from Mr. David 
R. Porter, International Secretary for the High School Boys, put 
new zeal and enthusiasm into the work. He addressed a mass 
meeting of two hundred boys, on the “Value of Bible Study,” and 
98 boys signed enrollment cards at this meeting. Addresses were 
also made by him at the Montreal High School, the Commercial 
and Technical High School, and Lower Canada College. 

During the year 12 Bible Classes were conducted, with 164 boys 
enrolled, and with an average attendance of 92. Two normal 
Classes for leaders were also held. If we might mention the one 
encouraging feature of the Bible Work in this Department this year, 
it would be the work of the four Classes from the High School, 
which met every Thursday evening for tea, and held Classes immedi- 
ately following. .The average attendance at these was 35. 

Besides the regular Physical work carried on, special mention 
ought to be made of the Summer Camp, held from June 19th to 
July 17th, and attended by 23 business boys, and 43 school boys. 


19 


31 boys decided for the Christian life at the two special meetings 
held at the School Boys’ Camp. 

Mention has already been made of the 108 boys enrolled in the 
Educational Classes. 82 boys wrote on the International exam- 
inations. 

Besides these activities a number of snowshoe tramps, sleigh 
drives and suppers, and entertainments have been held. The 
Christmas entertainment held for the Business Boys, at which 
about one hundred attended, might be specially mentioned. 


Social Department 


Gro. LyMAN, Chairman. 
W. J. Horiipay, Secretary 


One of the compelling motives which forced Sir George Williams 
to form an organization, later known as the Young Men’s Christian 
Association, was his craving for friendship and sociability. Many 
a young man in Montreal is craving for that same fellowship to- 
night. This the Young Men’s Christian Association is trying to 
supply. Every Department reports progress in the social activities. 
In addition to the regular social work within the several Depart- 
ments, among other activities might be mentioned: 

Billiard Room.—Two American tables and one Hnglish table, 
upon the recommendation of the Social Committee, were installed 
last fall, for the use of the membership. The tables are very 
’ popular, having been used on an average of over three hundred 
times a month. The Social Committee believe this innovation has 
been a most satisfactory and successful one. 


Bowling.—The two alleys in the basement have been open every 
evening, and Saturday afternoons during the year. Interest was 
very keen, and six teams were organized, and played in competition 
during the winter. 


The Reading Room on the first floor has been very popular— 
nearly all the well-known English and American magazines being 
kept on file. It is not an uncommon sight to see thirty men enjoying 
this room together. 

Lunch Room.—Mention should also be made of this Department 
of sociability. During the past few months this room has become 
very popular, until now between ninety and a hundred dinners are 
being served daily. 

Among the big banquets held should be mentioned the Thanks- 
giving supper, enjoyed by 150 men, representing fourteen nation- 
alities; the new Year’s reception, attended by nearly one thousand 
persons during the day, and enjoyed by all present; the Educational 
banquet, on March 8ist, which one hundred men attended; the 
Physical Department banquet, attended and enjoyed, April 19th, by 
125 men. 

Strangers’ Tea—The report of the Social Committee would not 
be complete without a word about the Strangers’ Tea, held every 
Sunday evening at 5.15, for the strangers within the city. This 
little tea has been conducted for many years by the Association, 
and with great success. Thousands of men throughout Canada 
have caught their first vision of Canada as a Christian nation at 
these little teas. More than seven hundred strangers, many of 


20 


them spending their first Sunday in Canada, have enjoyed the 
hospitality of the Young Men’s Christian Association at these 
strangers’ teas during the year just closed. 


Ladies’ Auxiliary 
In all these social activities, the Ladies’ Auxiliary has done 
splendid service, having taken charge of the ten large banquets, and 
assisted at numerous others. The work could not have been accom- 
plished at all but for the help of the Auxiliary. Their total receipts 


for the year were $476.30, and their expenditure $299.12, thereby 
showing a balance to their credit of $177.18. 


Staff Changes 


Several changes have taken place, or will take place in the 
near future. 

In March we welcomed Mr. J. F. Sinclair, of Minneapolis, to 
take the Assistant Secretaryship under Mr. Budge. 

In June Mr. J. W. Estey, of the University of New Brunswick, 
joined to take up the office work of the Central Association. 

Next month Mr. K. J. Hollinshead, of Albion College, Michigan, 
will take up the Boys’ Secretaryship, which Mr. Murray Brooks 
resigned to go as Strathcona Hall’s representative in the Foreign 
Work in Ceylon. 

The Central Association will also lose, with regret, Mr. Holli- 
day’s services, as in the early Fall he goes as Secretary to the 
Fairmount Branch, preparing the way for the larger work in the 
Annex, which the new building will entail. 


Conclusion 


This brief report does not give a complete idea of what the 
Association has accomplished this year for the men and boys of this 
city, but it does give a faint conception of the possibilities of this 
great movement. All the Secretaries have been kept busy with 
conferences, personal conversations with men, and with personal 
calls upon men in their rooms. : 

As Chairman of the Central Committee of Management I want 
to publicly thank all the Secretaries and Committeemen for their 
splendid support and help in the work during the year just closed. 
With a few exceptions every man has done what was expected of 
him in a remarkably efficient way. To these men the Association 
owes a great debt, and to many others, who, although not Com- 
mitteemen, or officers, have believed in our work, and have given 
of their time, talent, or money; we take this occasion to thank 
these men, because it is around such men that a healthy public 
spirit and sentiment is created. 

To the members of the Ladies’ Auxiliary, who have been so kind 
during the past year, we give our heartiest thanks. The work could 
not have been done without their hearty co-operation and help. 

We cannot close this report without expressing our heartfelt 
thanks to our beloved General Secretary, Mr. Budge, for carrying 
out the work so successfully—while nearly the whole of the year 
carrying the work of two men, His Christian spirit has been a 
source of great inspiration to us all. Our closing» word is our 
earnest prayer that he may continue in the vigor of mind and body, 
and give us added inspiration for many years to come. 


GERALD W. BIRKS, 
21 Chairman.

FAIRMOUNT AVENUE BRANCH 


EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE 


W. A. Witson. . . Chairman 

A. E. SHaw. . . . Vice-Chairman 

JupcE S. P. Leer. .Chairman of Finance Committee 
H. R. MacGregor. . Treasurer 


G. W. Evxiorr. . . . Recording Secretary 
C. S. WALLACE. . . . Chairman of Educational Committee 
TE LOAN & syccai Gate Chairman of Social Committee 

R. L, CHARLTON P. A. Dore R. J. LATIMER 

S. W. CurHBERT G. R. MacGrecor C. McFarLanp 

T. J. STEVENSON J. S. PARKE 


The Committee of Management of the Fairmount Avenue 
Branch Young Men’s Christian Association beg to submit the follow- 
ing general report of the work done at the Branch during the year 
1909-10. 


Dealing with the work by departments, the various Committees 
report as follows: 


Membership 


Mr. C. S. Watrace, Chairman. 


We are pleased to be able to report that, notwithstanding the 
lack of accommodation and attractions, 50% of our Seniors, and 
70% of our Juniors have renewed their tickets. 80% of the sub- 
scriptions falling due have been renewed, and in many cases 
increased amounts. The memberships are divided as follows: 
Seniors 127, Juniors 100, Subscribers 76, giving a total of 303—81 
of the 127 Seniors being church members. 


Religious 
Mr. A. E. SHaw, Chairman. 


From October ist, to April 30th, two mass meetings were 
held each week—for men on Sunday afternoons, and for boys on 
Friday evenings. Three Bible Classes were conducted—one for 
Intermediate members, and two for Juniors. Owing to the fact that 
the various churches in our neighborhood have a strong work for 
young men it was not thought wise to organize a Men’s Bible Class 
this year. The Committee are planning to make this a feature of 
the work next season. 


25 


Physical 


Mr. Gro. R. MacGrecor, Chairman. 


The Physical Department, although very much handicapped as 
regards space and equipment, has conducted successful work for 
both men and boys. The boys’ work has been especially progressive. 

Out of 107 men entitled to use the Physical Department 50 did 
so, while 81 of the 93 boys eligible availed themselves of the 
privileges offered. 

121 men and boys were enrolled, and 203 class sessions were 
held, with a total attendance of 3,118. 

The organized teams are ag follows: All round athletics, 3 
teams; baseball, 3 teams; basketball, 3 teams. Total enrollment in 
these teams being 61, men and boys. The total attendance at all 
physical privileges was 3,650. 

Junior, Intermediate, and Senior Basketball teams participated 
in City League schedules; the Junior and Intermediate teams 
winning the championship in their respective leagues, without losing 
a game. The Basketball teams played games in Ottawa Y.M.C.A., 
Sherbrooke Y.M.C.A., and Macdonald College, St. Anne’s. 


Social 


Mr. Harry SLoan, Chairman. 


Twenty-nine social events have been conducted during the year, 
with a total attendance of 1,135. The most important feature of the 
work accomplished by this Department during the year was the 
forming of a Ladies’ Auxiliary. This Auxiliary has been organized 
on similar lines to that of the Central Y.M.C.A. Auxiliary. Too 
much credit cannot be given to the ladies for the splendid service 
they have rendered since their organization, January 19th, 1910. 
The Auxiliary has at present 30 members on the roll, and it is 
expected that next year will see 100 ladies engaged in this very 
helpful service for the young men and boys. 


Boys’ Department 


Mr. Gro. W. Extiorr, Chairman. 


Splendid progress has been made in the Boys’ Work during the 
past year, and with the increased accommodation of a new building 
this work apparently has no limit to its possibilities. 

Mr. Frank T. Ritchie, Canadian Boys’ Work Secretary, visited 
the Association during the year, and a Boys’ Cabinet, which has 
practically controlled the work of the Department during the season, 
and a Bible Study Teachers’ Training Class are two of the marked 
results of Mr, Ritchie’s visit. 

30 boys of the 100 in the membership are enrolled on committees, 
The average attendance at the Older Boys’ meetings on Friday 
evenings, has been 35. The membership in the Department is com- 
posed as follows: 26 High School boys, 42 Junior School boys, and 
32 employed boys. 


26 


Perhaps the most encouraging feature of the season’s work was 
the successful conducting of a Boys’ Camp, on Lac Manitou, during 
the month of July. A splendid location was secured, and 52 took 
advantage of the opportunity to spend a pleasant holiday on one 
of the most beautiful Laurentian Lakes. A fee of $11.00 for two 
weeks, and $20 for a month, including all expenses, was charged, 
and $265 was contributed to the funds of the Association through 
this agency. 


Finance 
Mr. P. A. Dota, Chairman. 


We cannot conceive of a Young Men’s Christian Association 
without a Membership and Finance Committee. We began our 
report with a summary of the work of the Membership Committee, 
and we are bringing the account to a close with the report of the 
Finance Committee’s work during the year. The receipts for the 
year have been as follows: 


Membershipaic: ..2en. be oe iasd ted, neny sate 00L 00 
1 Diet 23): eect Aa e ae. Se ee 59 76 00 
Siihbseriptions.. =~... <phase. eens 400 
Sndiless ae. tae oe a eae ee. Se BOO.

Wot alien, Sao Kae ee al athe eRe ORO. 


The expenditure for the maintenance of the work has been 
$1,958.00. 

Leaving a balance on hand of $46.00. 

Your Committee appreciate the confidence which the Metropolitan 
Board has expressed in our work in such a substantial way, namely, 
the buying of a lot, and the proposed erection of a splendid building 
at the corner of Park Avenue and St. Viateur Street. We hope and 
pray that the work in this section may prove a boon to the young 
men and boys of the neighborhood, and that the manly Christian 
characters of its members may testify to the Board that the con- 
fidence reposed in the Committee was not misplaced. 


Respectfully submitted, 


W. A. MacLAREN, 
Secretary. 


W. A. WILSON, 
President.

RAILROAD BRANCH 


POINT. ST. CHARLES 


OFFICERS AND COMMITTEE OF MANAGEMENT

COMMITTEE 

C. MANNING W. S. CoprinG 

H. A. WHITE W. C. Murray 

S. PucH Frep. Evans 

H. N. CHAUVIN WALTER HyMAN 

G. J. SMirH Rost. SURGEON 


EXECUTIVE OFFICERS 


Davip THOMPSON. ..... Secretary 
Fc ee BRON a ae _. . Assistant Secretary 
A. C. JOHNSON .. 5... Physical Director 


In presenting the eleventh Annual Report of the Committee of 
Management we desire to praise Him, from whom cometh all good 
and perfect gifts, for the innumerable blessings that have been 
bestowed upon us during the past year, and to express our sincerest 
appreciation of the practical assistance and valuable support of the 
many members, friends, and contributors. 

With the gradual disappearance of the financial depression our 
Association’s finances continue to improve, and we have much 
pleasure in reporting that the small deficit carried over from last 
year has been wiped out, and we commence our new year with a 
balance, on the right side of $49.50. 


Religious Department 
Mr. S. Pucu, Chairman. 


57 Men’s meetings were held, and 113 sessions of Bible Study. 
Hight open air meetings were conducted. Total attendance at all 
meetings 5,654, an increase over last year of 28*/. 

Physical Director Johnson conducted a Junior Bible Study 
class every Saturday morning. 

Assistant Secretary Mercer is leader of the Intermediate Bible 
Study Class held every Thursday evening at 7.15. 


30 


Men’s Sunday Morning Bible Class at 10 o’clock is conducted by 
Secretary Thompson. This class is particularly for the men who 
room in the building. 

Sunday afternoon Gospel Meetings for men have been very well 
attended, and our whole religious work has been a very great 
source of encouragement. 


Educational Department 
Mr. CHAS. MANNING, Chairman. 


54 students were enrolled in seven subjects, as follows: Tele- 
graphy, Bookkeeping, Shorthand, Typewriting, French, Arithmetic, 
and Business Correspondence. 602 sessions were held, with an 
attendance of 2,216. 

Our Telegraph School continues to afford a splendid opportunity 
for young men who are anxious to become efficient in this branch 
of service. Several of our students have secured good positions in 
the railway company’s service, and our sincerest thanks are due 
the officers of the telegraph departments of the Grand Trunk and 
Canadian Pacific Railways for their courtesy and assistance. 

Our Bookkeeping and Shorthand Classes have eclipsed all previ- 
ous records, both in attendance and study. Four of our students 
passed the International examinations with honors, and will, in due 
course, receive their diplomas. This again brings to our notice the 
fact that Point St. Charles has the material from which a splendid 
educational work can be built up. 

The Literary and Debating Club has been the means of stimu- 
lating much interest in many important subjects. 

The present need of the Association is a properly equipped 
reading room. $200.00 has been set aside for this purpose, and we 
hope to have this amount augmented to such an extent as to 
furnish in a suitable manner a room that can properly be termed 
a Reading Room. 


Physical Department 


Mr. H. N. Cuavvin, Chairman. 


The work in this department has gone on with leaps and bounds. 
During the month of September the Gymnasium was overhauled, 
and put in first class condition, thus enabling the regular physical 
classes to commence on the 15th, two weeks earlier than in previous 
years. 

In October a Wrestling Club was organized. This proved to be 
quite an attraction to many of the members. The club closed the 
season with a tournament amongst its members, which was 
enthusiastically taken hold of. A nominal fee was charged for 
membership, and the club closed the season with a balance on hand 
of fifteen dollars. 


The Swimming Club was re-organized and put on a strong work- 
ing basis. Several handicap races took place, which proved very 
interesting and enjoyable. 


Basket Ball—aA great interest was shown in basket ball, with 
the result that two senior teams were entered in the City League, 


31 


and two boys’ teams in our Intermediate Association League. 
Later in the season an Association League was formed, which 
consisted of four teams, two from the Senior and two from the 
Business and Office Men’s Classes. The games created much in- 
terest, and a large number of spectators witnessed the matches, 
which were strongly contested. The “Nuggets” team won the 
“Evans” Cup, donated for the winners, and were presented with the 
same at the Annual Concert. 


A Snowshoe Club was organized for the first time, in the 
latter part of October, and has closed a very successful season, 
having over twenty members enrolled. 

During the month of March our Out-door Clubs were re-organized, 
and at the present time we have the following summer clubs con- 
nected with our Association, viz.: One Football Club, two Baseball 
Clubs, one Tennis Club, and one Swimming Club. 


The Bowling Club has put in a very busy season. Three teams 
were entered in the City Leagues, and finished the season well up 
in the front. The Senior team were in the semi-finals but failed 
to secure the much-desired trophy by a small margin. The club 
entered a five-man team in the M.A.A.A. tournament, and the boys 
succeeded in bringing home a splendid cup, being the second prize 
awarded for this contest. From March 16th to April 22nd, a 
tournament was conducted by our club, and was very successfully 
carried out. 

Total enrollment of the Physical Department for the year was 
258, having held 430 sessions, with a total attendance of 5,888, an 
increase over last year of 841. 


The membership keeps up to the 500 mark. 

The bed rooms were used 15,237 times, while upwards of 40,000 
meals were served in the restaurant. 

We take this opportunity of thanking the Central Board of 
Directors, and General Secretary, Mr. D. A, Budge, for the co- 
operation and helpful assistance received during the year. 


GENERAL. 


During the year many changes have taken place in the staff. 
In the month of September, Mr. A. C. Johnson, of the Toronto West 
End Y.M.C.A., became Physical Director, to succeed Mr. H. B. 
Anderson, resigned. In the month of November Secretary Mr. F. 
C. McGonigle resigned, and Mr. Allan Thompson was appointed 
Acting Secretary until January ist, when Mr. David Thompson 
assumed the duties of Secretary. Mr. Allan Thompson, in the mean- 
time, was called to the Allandale R.R.Y.M.C.A., and the position of 
Assistant Secretary was filled by Mr. J. R. Mercer, who had been 
atting for several months as Night Secretary. 


Respectfully submitted, 


W. A. KNEELAND, 
Chairman.
